test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Machinist) Official Paper (Held On: 06 May, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is not a component of a Vernier caliper?
solution:
**Concept**

 
• A Vernier caliper is a precision instrument used to measure internal and external dimensions as well as the depth of an object.
 
• Standard components of a Vernier caliper include the main scale, vernier scale, internal jaws, external jaws, depth measuring blade, and locking screw.
 
• An anvil is a stationary measuring face found on a **micrometer screw gauge**, not a Vernier caliper.

**Components of a Vernier Caliper**

The main parts of a Vernier caliper are:

 
• **Main Scale:** The large scale that runs along the body of the beam.
 
• **Vernier Scale:** The small sliding scale that provides the incremental measurement.
 
• **Outer Jaws:** Used to measure the external diameter or width of an object.
 
• **Inner Jaws:** Used to measure the internal diameter of objects like pipes.
 
• **Depth Probe:** A rod used to measure the depth of holes or steps.
 
• **Locking Screw:** Used to fix the position of the jaws once the measurement is taken to ensure accuracy while reading.

**Explanation**

By analyzing the components:

 
• **Locking Screw:** This is a standard part of a Vernier caliper used to tighten the sliding scale in place.
 
• **Main Scale:** This is the primary scale of the instrument.
 
• **Anvil:** In the context of precision measurement, an "anvil" refers to the fixed measuring face of a micrometer screw gauge. In general mechanical terms, an anvil is a heavy block used for forging metal. Neither of these uses pertains to the construction of a Vernier caliper.

**Hence, the anvil is not a component of a Vernier caliper.**</p
